name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Implement a standardized risk assessment template across all departments, led by the Risk Management team. This will enable consistent risk evaluation and reporting, making it easier to identify and address high-risk areas collaboratively. The trade-off is the initial investment of time and resources to train staff and modify existing processes, but the long-term benefits include improved communication and quicker decision-making regarding risk management.

name: Scriv
text: Risk Management’s template risks locking teams into rigid categories that miss context-specific threats. A better fix: require every department to log their top three risks weekly in a shared tracker, led by Operations—this forces real-time visibility without upfront design work. Settle it by piloting the tracker for two weeks and measuring whether it surfaces risks faster than the template.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt Risk Management’s standardized template, led by Risk Management. It guarantees consistent risk language across departments, cutting confusion in cross-team escalations. The trade-off is slower initial adoption for long-term clarity, but that’s worth it—rigid categories beat ad-hoc guessing when lives and budgets are on the line.
[dispatched 4 workers: worker-1993, worker-6145, worker-3978… — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: Risk Management’s template locks teams into yesterday’s risks. Operations’ shared tracker forces real-time visibility but risks drowning in noise—no one will read 50 weekly entries. Settle it by piloting Operations’ tracker for 30 days, then forcing Risk Management to audit the top 10 escalated risks and refine the template based on actual gaps.
